WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback

paper.arxiv.2112.09332

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2112.09332v3. Human-comparison reward training and citation-cherry-picking limitations establish training/evaluation protocol scope. Human preference remains distinct from factual truth and safe deployment. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Reference-answer comparisons have blinding, answer-intent and factual-checking limitations; citation-bearing answers can seem more authoritative and training can incentivize cherry-picked convincing references rather than a fair assessment of evidence.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

WebGPT trained GPT-3-family models using human browser demonstrations, comparison-trained reward models, PPO or rejection sampling to generate answers with collected web references.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The study collected about 6, 000 demonstrations and 21, 500 answer comparisons, mostly ELI5; around 25% of data came from 10 Upwork contractors and 75% from 46 Surge AI contractors. Paid trials, manual checks and reference-support annotations were used for QC.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

On ELI5 evaluation, the 175B best-of-64 model was preferred to human demonstrator answers 56% of the time and to ELI5 reference answers 69%, counting ties as 50%; the reference-answer comparison stripped citations and used new contractors with minimal instructions.
